newsitem.title: USA: Sizzler International files reorganization plan.
newsitem.headline: Sizzler International files reorganization plan.

text.p: Sizzler International Inc. said Monday it has filed a plan of reorganization and hopes to emerge from bankruptcy by June 1.
Sizzler, based in Los Angeles, said it planned full payment of creditors' claims, estimated at about $70 million, to be secured by international operations.

"We're on the road now. My expectation is (a return to profitability) in the next fiscal year," said Chief Financial Officer Christopher Thomas in an interview. "We've completed the restructuring of our U.S. operations, and we're really prepared to move forward now."
Thomas said he expected the restaurant chain to return to profitability as early as the first quarter of fiscal 1998, which starts May 1.

Sizzler filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in June, closing 130 unprofitable restaurants and taking a charge of $109 million. Thomas said he did not expect any more charges from the reorganization even though the company closed more restaurants than it had initially planned.
Thomas said a court hearing on the plan of reorganization is expected on April 21 and pending all required approvals the company should exit bankruptcy on June 1.

Sizzler will be even leaner than originally planned. At the start of February the company operated 71 domestic restaurants and 201 franchise operations. Internationally the firm operates 42 Sizzlers and has 92 franchises, three joint-ventures as well as 94 Kentucky Fried Chicken restaurants in Queensland, Australia.
In June Sizzler said it would keep 85 domestic restaurants and 235 franchises.
Sizzler's stock rose 12.5 cents to $2.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
